bug_semantics: The in-process TURN server's UDP receive loop is unsupervised and does not isolate datagram processing. ReceiveUdpAsync() wraps only the socket ReceiveAsync in an inner try; HandleUdpDatagram() runs inside the while body but outside any per-datagram handler, and the generic catch (Exception) sits lexically outside the while. A single unauthenticated UDP datagram whose STUN header first byte is 0x80-0xFF makes STUNHeader.ParseSTUNHeader throw ApplicationException; the exception unwinds past the loop, the outer catch logs it and the method returns. Start() launches the loop fire-and-forget (_ = ReceiveUdpAsync()) with no restart logic, so the TURN UDP relay stays dead for every client until process restart — a pre-authentication whole-server denial of service. A second path (too-short datagram with an accepted first byte -> null header -> NullReferenceException in ParseSTUNMessage) exists; the advisory documents the first.

The file did not exist in the parent tree (4b9732a2fb4f776f375f5a4f1e220b5943ef92a5), so the defective loop is written by this single commit.
